issues.legal_issue: A widow who receives property under a will granting only a life interest does not acquire an absolute estate in that property under the Hindu Succession Act.
material_facts: The property owner’s genuine last will gave his widow a life interest in his estate and directed that it pass to collateral relatives after her death.
The widow later made a will purporting to leave the property to her daughter.
The daughter claimed title under the widow’s later will.
issues.conclusion: The widow’s interest remained a life estate and did not become absolute under the Hindu Succession Act; she therefore could not pass title to the daughter under her will, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Hindu Succession Act does not enlarge a limited life interest expressly given to a widow under a will into an absolute estate. The Court relied on the Act’s provisions concerning a Hindu woman’s property; it cited no earlier cases.

predicates.testamentary_succession_title_dispute: The dispute concerns title to property claimed through testamentary succession.
predicates.property_received_under_will: The widow received the property under a will.
predicates.will_grants_only_life_interest: The will gave the widow only a life interest in the property.
predicates.later_claimant_claims_through_widows_wil: A later claimant bases title on a will made by the widow.
predicates.limited_will_interest_not_enlarged_to_ab: The life interest given by the will remains limited and does not become an absolute estate.

issues.definition: When a title dispute concerns property received by a widow under a will that grants only a life interest, and a later claimant relies on the widow’s will, the limited interest remains limited rather than becoming absolute.
